content.title: About
content.content: Rice croquettes are small fried or baked balls made from cooked rice, often mixed with cheese, herbs, and spices. They have a golden, crispy crust and a soft, flavorful interior. Croquettes are enjoyed as a snack, side dish, or component of Asian and European cuisines.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rice croquettes originated in Japan as a lighter alternative to traditional potato croquettes.
To achieve a crunchy exterior, they are usually coated in breadcrumbs or cornmeal before cooking.
Vegetarians and vegans replace cheese with plant‑based alternatives to keep the dish fully plant‑based.
In many countries they are served with teriyaki sauce, soy sauce, or sweet chili dip.
Proper freezing preserves taste and texture for up to three months.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice provides a steady release of energy, helping maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Low fat content when baked
items.content: Baked croquettes contain less saturated fat than deep‑fried versions.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Rice supplies thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Contains fiber (when whole‑grain rice is used)
items.content: Fiber supports digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Can be protein‑enriched
items.content: Adding cheese, tofu, or legumes turns croquettes into a good source of animal or plant protein.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese‑filled croquettes may trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: High sodium in sauces
items.content: Serving with soy sauce or other salty dips should be done in moderation to avoid excess salt.

items.title: Frying increases calorie density
items.content: Deep‑fried croquettes contain more fat and calories, which may be undesirable for weight management.

items.title: Risk of bacterial growth if stored improperly
items.content: Cooked croquettes should be refrigerated within two hours and kept no more than 2‑3 days to prevent bacterial contamination.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve rice croquettes hot as an appetizer, alongside meat or fish dishes, or tossed into salads. They pair well with teriyaki sauce, sweet chili, yogurt dip, or plain sour cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool croquettes to room temperature, then place in an airtight container. Store in the refrigerator for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat in the oven or microwave to restore the crisp crust.
